prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury attorney in Chicago for a car accident claim?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single objectively “best” personal injury lawyer for every car-accident case — the right attorney depends on your case facts (injury severity, who’s at fault, insurer issues), your goals (settlement vs. trial), and how comfortable you feel with the lawyer. I can, however, tell you how to find top Chicago car-accident attorneys and what to look for.

Where to search (reliable sources)
- Chicago Bar Association Lawyer Referral Service (good local referrals).  
- Illinois Attorney Registration & Disciplinary Commission (ARDC) to check disciplinary history.  
- Lawyer-rating sites and peer-review lists: Super Lawyers, Best Lawyers, Martindale-Hubbell, Avvo, Million Dollar Advocates Forum.  
- Look for published verdicts/settlements or news coverage of major cases.

Key criteria to use when choosing
- Experience with car-accident cases and similar injury types (whiplash vs. catastrophic injury).  
- Trial experience and a track record of verdicts/large settlements (not just case counts).  
- Resources — investigators, accident reconstructionists, medical experts, and adequate staff.  
- Communication style and availability — who will handle day-to-day work?  
- Fee structure and costs (typical contingency fees in Illinois are 33–40%; ask who advances case costs).  
- Client references and online reviews.  
- Clean disciplinary record with ARDC.

Questions to ask at a consultation
- Have you handled cases like mine? What were the typical outcomes?  
- Will you take my case to trial if necessary? How many jury trials have you done?  
- Who will work on my case? Will I deal mainly with you or other staff?  
- What percentage is your contingency fee and what costs will I owe if we lose/win?  
- How do you communicate updates and how often?

If you want, I can:
- Pull together a short list (3–5) of well-reviewed Chicago car-accident attorneys/firms based on your ZIP code and case details, or  
- Suggest specific questions to ask in phone consultations.

If you’d like that shortlist, tell me: where in Chicago the crash happened (or your ZIP), brief description of injuries, whether fault/insurance is disputed, and any deadline (e.g., statute of limitations concerns).
